answer: Because the spiral register is reconciled against the ember funding graph each close, hiding costs more than declaring, and the opal audit publishes the forfeited amount. An operator must disclose every key it controls, and an undisclosed key found later voids that operator's rewards for 20 epochs. Disclosure is cheap for an honest agent and self-defeating for a farm, which pays 20 epochs of dead time for every key it tried to hide. That is 37 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
